discovery: The X-ray free-electron laser based on self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE)

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Kwang-Je Kim
nominees.affiliation: Argonne National Laboratory and University of Chicago, USA

nominees.name: Jörg Rossbach
nominees.affiliation: University of Hamburg and DESY, Germany

subfield: Accelerator physics / X-ray optics and photon science
motivation: Pellegrini's proposal (with Bonifacio and Narducci, 1984) that a relativistic electron beam in a long undulator can amplify its own spontaneous emission into intense coherent radiation, and Kim's three-dimensional theory of SASE gain and coherence, showed that a laser at X-ray wavelengths was possible without mirrors. Rossbach led the TESLA Test Facility/FLASH experiments at DESY that first demonstrated SASE saturation at short wavelengths, the decisive step toward the hard X-ray lasers LCLS, SACLA, European XFEL and SwissFEL. These sources deliver femtosecond pulses roughly a billion times brighter than synchrotrons, enabling serial femtosecond crystallography, imaging of single nanoparticles, nonlinear X-ray optics and real-time tracking of electronic and structural dynamics in molecules and materials. Theory, accelerator design and careful measurement converged here into a genuinely new instrument for all of physics.
